question: When the player first fought the Great Sage Remnant (大圣残躯), which of the following Magic Treasures (法宝) did they use? 1. Fire Shield (避火罩) 2. Dingfeng Pearl (定风珠) 3. Banana Leaf Fan (芭蕉扇) 4. Embroidered Needle (绣花针)?

rollouts.answer: 4. Embroidered needle (绣花针), citing a needle-like golden beam at ~83490-83492s.

db_evidence.notes: The literal clue_interval (83305-83311) sits inside a long, continuous, visually noisy boss-fight sequence (~82920-83610s) whose auto-generated 30sec episode captions describe generic combat/fire/particle effects and do not name the treasure explicitly; the boss identity text ('大圣残躯'/大圣残魂) only appears in a nearby cutscene caption (83220-83250s) and faintly on the in-fight boss-name HUD bar. The treasure identity is retrievable, but only via two indirect visual sources outside the literal clue window: (1) the pre-fight equipment menu at ~80280-80320s, which explicitly labels 芭蕉扇 as 已装备 (equipped) with its official activation description, and (2) a distinctive whirlwind/tornado combat effect around 82956-82969s matching that description. Both are well before the stated clue_interval, meaning the clue_interval metadata marks only one moment of the fight, not the moment where the treasure choice is most legible.

root_causes: Two rollouts (2 and 0) failed at the visual-interpretation step, not the retrieval step: rollout 2 used the correct time window but the clip_qa sub-agent hallucinated/misread an equipment-wheel 'fire shield vessel' icon in a frame that in fact shows no open menu, just ordinary mid-combat HUD and fire particle effects.

Rollout 0 anchored its clip_qa window too late (83370-83520s, after the clue_interval and after the fan's whirlwind activation at ~82956-82969s), landing on a different visual effect later in the same continuous encounter (a needle-like beam near 83490s) and misidentified it as the answer treasure.

The three successful rollouts (1, 3, 4) succeeded via two different but both effective evidence sources: reading an explicit equip-status text label in the pre-fight menu (unambiguous), or correctly matching a mid-fight visual effect (whirlwind) to the treasure's known canonical activation description (less ambiguous than rollout 2's fire-icon misread because the whirlwind is visually very distinctive).

The database's auto-captioned episodes text is too generic during fast, visually busy boss-fight footage to resolve which of four similar-looking magic treasures was used; all five rollouts correctly fell back to clip_qa, so the split in scores comes down to clip_qa window choice and visual-recognition accuracy, not SQL/semantic-search retrieval failure.
what_worked: Targeting the pre-fight equipment/menu screen (~80280-80320s) where the game explicitly displays an 已装备 (equipped) text label for the treasure, removing ambiguity entirely (rollouts 1 and 3).

Matching an observed mid-combat visual effect (a sustained whirlwind/tornado) to the treasure's own official in-game activation description ('可扇出飓风') rather than guessing from a generic fire/particle burst (rollout 4).
transferable_lessons: For 'which item/treasure was used' questions, prioritize clip_qa on any equip/menu screen with explicit status text (已装备) over interpreting fast in-combat particle effects, since a menu label is unambiguous while combat VFX is easily confused between similar-looking treasures.

When a combat visual effect is the only available evidence, first retrieve the treasure's canonical activation description (via run_sql/semantic_search on object_states, semantic_triples, or topic_facts) and match the observed effect against that description, instead of asking the visual sub-agent to freely guess which HUD icon looks like which item.

Do not anchor clip_qa windows only to the literal clue_interval from question metadata when it falls inside a long continuous action sequence; scan slightly before/around it (including any equip/menu screens shortly before the encounter) since the moment that best resolves the answer may not be the moment tagged as the clue.

Cross-check a visual sub-agent's claim of seeing a specific HUD icon/menu by pulling the cited frame directly when the interpretation is decisive for the final answer; an icon claimed to be present but not actually visible in the frame is a concrete, checkable failure mode.
open_questions: Whether the '石猴' name shown on the boss health bar in the 82956-82969s frames refers to an earlier phase/alias of the same '大圣残躯' boss or a genuinely distinct preceding encounter was not fully resolved from captions alone; this does not change the treasure-identification conclusion (both rollouts 2 and 4 targeted the same window) but affects precise boss-identity bookkeeping.

Whether the needle-like beam effect rollout 0 observed at ~83490s corresponds to a real secondary treasure use later in the same encounter (e.g., embroidered needle used after the fan) was not independently confirmed; if so, the question/reference answer implicitly means 'first treasure used' rather than 'only treasure used', which rollout 0 did not account for.
